subtype_info: pulmonary tuberculosis with cystic changes and pneumothorax
title: Cystic lung tuberculosis in children: A series of five cases
case_text: A 7-year-old girl was admitted with complaints of fever over 3 weeks, tachypnoea and cough for 4 days. In view of the respiratory distress, the child was transferred to the paediatric intensive care unit on day 5 post-admission. Mycobacterium tuberculosis was detected on sputum GeneXpert evaluation, and ATT was initiated. On day 11, the child experienced a sudden exacerbation of her respiratory distress. The CXR (not shown) revealed a left pneumothorax, for which an ICD was inserted. Subsequent CECT chest (Figure 6) revealed extensive GGOs and confluent nodular opacities in both lungs with patchy consolidation in both lower lobes, along with small cysts and bronchiolar dilatation. Other CT findings were mediastinal lymphadenopathy, pulmonary interstitial emphysema in the left upper lobe, minimal left pneumothorax with a pleural effusion, hepatosplenomegaly and hypodense non-calcified granulomas in the liver and spleen. The spleen also demonstrated a few small wedge-shaped regions of non-enhancing parenchyma suggestive of old infarcts. The patient responded well to ATT and recovered.

   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Tuberculosis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: pulmonary tuberculosis with cystic changes and pneumothorax
